Welcome to lesson fourteen, Docker Compose! With Compose, you write all your container settings in a file once, and then start everything with one short command.
Why do we need Compose? Your commands keep getting longer. Remember this one from lesson ten? A docker run with a name, a port, a volume, and an image.
It's hard to remember.
It's easy to mistype.
And it's hard to share with a teammate.
Docker Compose fixes all of this. You write it in a file once, then start everything with one short command.
A Compose project lives in its own folder. Let's make one.

One command stopped and deleted the container and the network, and your html folder is untouched. With Compose, the whole setup lives in compose dot yammel. Up dash d to start, down to remove. Run it again any time: same result, nothing to remember.

Congratulations, you used Docker Compose! Compose dot yammel holds your containers' settings. Docker compose up dash d creates and starts everything in the background. Docker compose P S lists this project's containers. And docker compose down stops and deletes the containers and the network.
